episode_title: Embracing Collective Success with Collaborative Accreditation with Dr. Roberta Ross-Fisher

real_qa.q: What is the difference between developing a culture of continuous program improvement versus a culture of compliance in accreditation preparation?
real_qa.r: There is a big difference between the two. A culture of continuous program improvement rather than compliance is crucial for a program and ideally an entire institution. The culture that you establish will impact how successful you are in your accreditation efforts and will also impact your outcomes and student success.
real_qa.requete: continuous program improvement versus compliance culture accreditation

real_qa.q: How should institutions organize accreditation roles to avoid risk of losing critical data if a single person leaves?
real_qa.r: Rather than designate one or two people or a handful of people for your accreditation efforts, create a schema for your accreditation efforts and include an organizational chart rather than listing individuals to serve in those key roles. This protects against scenarios where key data is stored on a personal laptop or the person leaves the institution.
real_qa.requete: accreditation organizational structure avoid single person risk

real_qa.q: What is a quality assurance system in the context of higher education accreditation?
real_qa.r: A quality assurance system is not a software program or a website. Instead, a quality assurance system is a well-planned and well-executed system which is designed to monitor quality on key performance indicators.
real_qa.requete: what is quality assurance system definition higher ed

real_qa.q: What is the relationship between state program approvals and programmatic accreditation?
real_qa.r: State program approvals and programmatic accreditation really do intersect in a big way and are very dependent on each other in many states. In some states, you can have programmatic accreditation without state program approval, but this depends on the state and really does raise the stakes considerably.
real_qa.requete: state program approval versus programmatic accreditation relationship

real_qa.q: How should accreditors move toward competency-based evaluation models instead of binary met/not met standards?
real_qa.r: Rather than simply stating whether standards were met or not met, accreditors could rate institutions on a performance scale, kind of like on a rubric that reflects the extent to which each standard has been met, as well as specific performance indicators. This would enable colleges and universities to be creative and remain true to who they are as a unique institution.
real_qa.requete: competency-based rubric accreditation standards performance scale

real_qa.q: What challenges do institutions face when managing accreditation compliance across multiple states and accrediting bodies?
real_qa.r: All individual states are constantly reviewing and revising their requirements, many times on an annual basis, making it challenging to stay current on state regulations. Institutions also need to keep their ear to the ground to know what changes are coming up in the pipeline, especially for programs requiring state licensure like nursing or teaching.
real_qa.requete: state accreditation requirements annual changes compliance challenges

guest.bio_context: Dr. Roberta Ross-Fisher has extensive accreditation experience across multiple institution types including public, private, for-profit, nonprofit, secular, and faith-based institutions. She began her accreditation journey during her doctoral program by creating a framework for evaluating gifted programs across Missouri, and has since served as a teacher of the gifted, department chair, dean, and held a department role focused on compliance and accreditation at an institution serving students across all 50 US states and four US territories. She brings expertise in competency-based education and practical approaches to quality assurance.
